## TL;DR
- In the canton of Bern, the rules depend on the competent authority - Institutions and categories of students may have different rules - Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be checked on the official source
## Key facts
- Topic → university fees in the Canton of Bern - Differences → institutions and categories of students - Competence → canton, municipality or competent institution - Check → requirements, deadlines and amounts on the official source
### The starting point: competence
In the Canton of Bern, university fees must be read starting from the institution that manages the individual case. The framework indicated by the source distinguishes between canton, municipality and competent institution: one of these levels can be the reference for university fees and integration programs.
For those preparing a registration, this changes the search method. It is not enough to look for a figure referring generically to Bern: you need to identify the official source of the competent canton or university and check the requirements, deadlines and amounts on that page. The same attention is needed when comparing different categories of students or institutions.
One category of student may follow a different rule than another, while two institutions may refer to different offices. The item to note, therefore, is not just the amount: the applicable category, any exemption, the available contribution and the deadline within which to act are also part of the verification. The official source remains the first step of registration.
The topic is part of the broader autonomy of the Cantons. In Switzerland there are three tax levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; the municipalities apply a multiplier on the cantonal tax. This fiscal architecture is used to read taxes, but does not in itself identify the university fee.
Even acronyms require a clear separation. The AFC/ESTV concerns direct federal tax and VAT; the cantonal administrations deal with cantonal and municipal taxes. The UFAS/BSV is linked to social security, including AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, and does not set taxes; the FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For university fees, the reference remains the cantonal, municipal or university body indicated by the official source.
For the budget of those living in Switzerland, the distinction is concrete: a university item may require cantonal or institutional control, while the other items have different channels. Looking for a single answer in a single office risks confusing skills and procedures. ## Compare rules, not just figures
### Four checks before estimating the cost
The differences between university fees in the Canton of Bern cannot be managed with a comparison based only on the final amount. The useful question is what combination of institution, category of student, and relevant authority produces that rule. This interpretation avoids transferring a deadline found elsewhere to another registration or considering a contribution provided by a single institution valid for everyone.
| Element | What to check | Why | |---|---|---| | Institution | official source of the competent body | the rule may change | | Category | applicable student category | different conditions may apply | | Exemption | requirements indicated by the source | the benefit must be verified | | Contribution | competent cantonal body or university | conditions and deadlines count |
If a person moves from one institution to another, the verification must be repeated on the new official source. If the student category changes, it is not enough to maintain the previous calculation: any exemptions, contributions, requirements and deadlines must be checked again. When a cantonal page refers to the competent university, the reference is part of the procedure and should not be replaced with information found on a different source.
The budget must also separate university fees from the cost of living and other administrative items. For residents, KVG/KVG is compulsory health insurance to be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums are per capita, vary by canton and region and may include a reduction in premiums through a cantonal subsidy. The KVG/KVG is neither a tax nor a salary contribution, therefore it should not be added or compared with the university fee as if it were the same item.
The same caution applies to social security. AVS/AHV, AI and BVG/BVG fall under social security, while the FSIO/BSV does not set taxes. Direct federal tax and VAT fall under the AFC/ESTV; cantonal and municipal taxes to cantonal administrations. Distinguishing these chapters allows us to better understand the cost of living without attributing to the individual university skills that belong to other bodies.
The correct comparison, therefore, is not between isolated numbers. It is between official source, applicable category, deadline and treatment expected for that specific registration. ## From verification to registration application
### Operating procedure
To transform information on university fees in the Canton of Bern into concrete practice, it is best to follow a short sequence that always refers to the official source.
1. Define the subject of the audit. Start from the registration and note whether the search concerns the tax, a possible exemption or a contribution. Keeping these elements separate avoids confusing an access condition with a reduction or support.
2. Identify the competent body. Check whether the reference page is that of the canton, municipality or university institution. If the first agency refers to another office, follow that referral and do not mix instructions from different sources.
3. Classify the student's position. The source predicts differences between categories of students and institutions; therefore the applicable category must be verified before reading amounts, requirements or conditions. Without this step, the comparison may refer to the wrong situation.
4. Record operational data. Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be obtained from the official source. The conditions for any exemptions and contributions must be sought in the same check. The useful data is not an isolated figure, but the combination of amount, term and requirement.
5. Double check before signing up. Before proceeding, compare the official page with the category identified and verify that the body indicated is the competent one. If the practice involves multiple levels, it maintains reference to each one without replacing the cantonal rule with that of another institution.
This procedure keeps the university fee separate from taxes and other expenses. For taxation, the AFC/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT, while the cantonal administrations deal with cantonal and municipal taxes. For pension provision, AVS/AHV and BVG/BVG belong to a different chapter. For those who are residents, the KVG/KVG must also be verified within three months of arrival, with rules on premiums and reductions managed at cantonal level.
After completing the checks, the comparison with the costo della vita in Svizzera helps place the university spending in the overall budget.

item.title: Watch and gold bar for Trump, Seco: “They were for the American people”
item.description: The gifts to Donald Trump were worth approximately 100'000 francs The delivery dates back to November 2025 US tariffs dropped from 39% to 15% A report on the authorities
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Gifts to Donald Trump were worth around 100'000 francs - The delivery dates back to November 2025 - US tariffs fell from 39% to 15% - A report on the federal authorities is expected by the end of the year
## Key facts - What → Rolex table clock and engraved gold bar - Indicated recipient → the American people - Who defended the initiative → Helene Budliger Artieda, director of Seco - Where → interview on the sidelines of an economic forum in New Delhi - Total value → approximately 100,000 francs - Legally binding agreement → talks still ongoing - Institutional review → Management Commission of the National Council - Expiration of the report → by the end of the year
### Seco's position
On October 14, 2026, Helene Budliger Artieda defended the gifts given to Donald Trump by a delegation of Swiss entrepreneurs. The director of Seco clarified that the initiative came from the private sector and that the watch and the ingot were not intended personally for the then 79-year-old president of the United States, but for the American people.
In an interview with Bloomberg TV, given on the sidelines of an economic forum in New Delhi, the outgoing secretary of state added that the gifts were registered at the White House. If all goes well, he explained, they will be destined for a presidential library. Budliger Artieda has resigned effective at the end of March 2027.
### The visit and the duties dossier
The delivery took place in November 2025, during a visit to the United States organized while the dispute over customs barriers was ongoing. The delegation went to Trump to negotiate and brought him a Rolex tabletop and an engraved gold bar, with a total value of around 100,000 francs.
The director described the participants as serious businessmen, convinced that they had acted within the framework of the legal provisions and after having carried out legal checks. Among them were Alfred Gantner, co-founder of Partners Group, Jean-Frédéric Dufour, number one at Rolex, and Johann Rupert, chairman of the board of directors of Richemont.
The matter remains open on a political-administrative level. The Management Commission of the National Council wants to examine the actions of the federal authorities in relation to American tariffs; the report is expected to be concluded by the end of the year. On the negotiation front, Seco says it is satisfied: since November 2025, when the reduction of US duties from 39% to 15% was announced, the United States has respected the agreement. Bern seeks security and calmer trade relations after the turbulent times following the tariff announcement on the so-called Liberation Day in April 2025. Talks for a legally binding agreement, however, continue. ## Practical reading for the Swiss economy
### The reference point for exporters
The figure that captures the change in the negotiations is the move in US tariffs from 39% to 15%, announced in November 2025. The source adds that the United States honored the agreement. For Swiss exporters, therefore, the concrete point is the level of the customs barrier specified in the negotiations, not the value of the gift delivered to the White House.
The two pieces of data belong to the same story but serve different functions: around 100'000 francs relate to the watch and gold bar; 39% and 15%, on the other hand, describe the reduction in US tariffs. Separating these elements prevents the delivery from being interpreted as an economic measure for residents. The source does not specify sectors, goods or companies and does not allow the effect to be extended to every Swiss activity. The group directly referred to is exporters, for whom Helene Budliger Artieda described conditions as difficult when stability is lacking in trade relations.
### Two timelines not to be confused
The dossier also has a second track. On the one hand, talks continue on a legally binding agreement between Switzerland and the United States; on the other, the National Council Control Committee is preparing a review of the federal authorities' actions in relation to US tariffs. The report is expected by the end of the year. The first track concerns the content of the trade barriers; the second concerns how the federal authorities handled the matter. The source does not yet present the outcome of either.
For those living in Switzerland, this distinction is the most solid practical takeaway: the text does not announce a new individual procedure. The effect described remains focused on trade relations and exporting companies. Bern is seeking certainty and calmer relations after the turbulent times that followed the tariff announcement of the so-called Liberation Day, in April 2025. As long as the legally binding agreement remains under discussion, the picture presented by the source is that of a reduction already announced and a negotiation that is still open. ## How to follow the dossier
### A five-step check
For a Swiss reader, the most concrete way to follow developments is to separate the information already available from the decisions still pending.
1. Identify which aspect of the news is involved. If the update concerns the watch, the gold bar or their registration at the White House, it refers to the private initiative delivered in November 2025. If it concerns the tariff percentage, it refers instead to the trade negotiations. 2. Check the tariff figure reported. The source uses the comparison between the initial 39% and the 15% announced after the agreement. This is the reference point not to be confused with the overall value of the gifts. 3. Verify the status of the agreement. The agreement on the reduction was honored by the United States, according to Budliger Artieda, but talks on a legally binding text are still ongoing. An update that refers to negotiations therefore does not amount, in the available text, to the conclusion of the agreement. 4. Follow parliamentary oversight. The Control Committee of the National Council is examining the actions of the federal authorities regarding US tariffs, and the report is expected by the end of the year. 5. Limit the conclusions to the parties mentioned. The source refers to Swiss exporters and trade relations with the United States; it does not mention forms, applications or personal deadlines for residents.
### What remains to be verified
This framework avoids two opposite errors: turning a private gift into a new economic measure or considering definitive a negotiation that the source still describes as open. For the Swiss exporters mentioned by the source, the issue to monitor is the customs barrier and any legally binding agreement; for the public, the institutional issue is the report on the actions of the federal authorities.
The available timeline remains clear: visit and gifts in November 2025, announcement of the tariff reduction in the same month, parliamentary report by the end of the year, and the director's resignation at the end of March 2027. These are the dates explicitly present for reconstructing developments, without adding procedures or effects that the source does not describe.

item.description: Attack on hundreds of French supermarkets Remote manipulation of refrigeration Damage amounting to millions of euros Coop and Migros: no similar attack recorded
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Attack on hundreds of French supermarkets - Refrigeration manipulated remotely - Damage amounting to millions of euros - Coop and Migros: no similar attack recorded
## Key facts - Target → refrigeration systems - Location → French supermarkets - Effect → higher temperatures and unusable food - Manufacturer → Danfoss, Danish company - Device status → obsolete generations without security updates - Switzerland → Coop and Migros have not recorded similar cases - Home → connected televisions, vacuum cleaners and speakers - Expert → Jean-Marc Seigneur, University of Geneva
A cyber attack that hit hundreds of French supermarkets has brought digital security into an infrastructure linked to food preservation. The pirates remotely manipulated the refrigeration systems, causing the temperature to rise.
Large quantities of food have thus become unusable. The damage caused by the attack amounted to millions of euros, according to the description of the episode.
The case reignites attention on the security of devices connected to the internet. The sequence described by the source is concrete: a system reached remotely was manipulated, the temperature rose and the food contents were no longer usable.
For the two Swiss chains the picture is different: Coop and Migros report not having encountered attacks of the same type. Migros adds that only a few of its stores use Danfoss refrigeration systems and that, for now, there are no signs of their involvement.
### The role of obsolete systems
The Danish manufacturer Danfoss, which makes many of the systems involved, explained that the affected devices are mainly of older generations and no longer benefit from security updates. The company thus drew attention to the conditions of the affected devices.
The threat also extends to private homes, where televisions, vacuum cleaners, speakers and other network-connected devices can provide an entry point for a cyber attack.
Connecting to the internet can leave any device exposed that does not have adequate protections and updates. The passage does not refer to a concrete domestic attack; instead, it signals possible exposure due to connection and insufficient protection.
This extension from commerce to homes is the national point of the story. Even for those living in Switzerland, the question is not just about refrigeration systems: it concerns the entire set of objects that can be connected to the network.
Jean-Marc Seigneur, an expert from the University of Geneva, recommends replacing default passwords, moving towards products from reliable companies and providing software and firmware updates. Finally, it invites us to evaluate whether it is really useful to make each device intelligent: each connected device introduces a further possible attack surface. ## Risk is not the same as an attack that has already occurred
The report makes it possible to distinguish three aspects. The first is the documented event: in French supermarkets, refrigeration systems were manipulated remotely, causing the temperature to rise and making food unusable. The second concerns the position of the Swiss companies mentioned: Coop and Migros have not reported similar attacks, while Migros currently has no indication that the few stores using Danfoss systems are involved. The third concerns homes: the source speaks of potential entry points, not a domestic attack that has already been documented.
### Three conditions to consider together
A device connected to the network is not automatically considered compromised. The source identifies a potential vulnerability when it is not adequately protected and updated. Danfoss's clarification adds a second element: a large share of the affected devices belongs to obsolete generations that no longer receive security updates. For the reader, the difference lies between the mere presence of a connection and the protection condition indicated in the source.
| Condition | Indication in the source | |---|---| | Device connected to the internet | May become a potential entry point | | Insufficient protection | The device may be vulnerable | | Now-obsolete generation | No longer receives security updates | | Making every device smart | Its actual usefulness should be assessed |
The relevant comparison for people living in Switzerland is not between an attack in France and a certainty in Switzerland. Coop and Migros have not reported similar cases, but the source does not present this fact as a guarantee for every connected device. At the same time, it does not describe a domestic attack that has already occurred: it mentions televisions, vacuum cleaners, speakers and other objects as potential entry points.
The practical consequence is a change in approach. The question is not only whether a device performs its function, but whether the connection provides a genuine benefit. Seigneur invites us to reflect on precisely this point: making every object smart introduces a new potential attack surface for every connected device. In this reading, the case of the French supermarkets becomes a reference point for assessing household choices without turning a possibility into an attack that has already been confirmed. ## The checklist for home appliances
The practical response indicated by the source consists of four guidelines for objects connected to the network. The sequence concerns both the appliances mentioned for homes and, more generally, any device connected to the internet: vulnerability depends on not being adequately protected and updated.
> “Replace default passwords, opt for products from reliable companies, and ensure that software and firmware are updated.”
### 1. Change the default password
The first check is to replace the default password. This measure should be considered for every object connected to the network, not just a refrigeration system. The source mentions televisions, vacuum cleaners, speakers and other household devices.
### 2. Choose a reliable company
When choosing a connected product, the expert recommends opting for reliable companies. This criterion is significant because Danfoss specified that a substantial share of the affected appliances comes from outdated generations that no longer receive security updates. The source does not provide a list of manufacturers or models: the guidance remains that of the expert, namely to favor reliable companies.
### 3. Keep software and firmware updated
The third step consists of keeping software and firmware updated. The recommendation concerns both, without separating software management from firmware management. For connected objects in the home, this is the indicated check for avoiding the vulnerability condition referred to by the source.
### 4. Assess whether the smart function is really needed
The fourth step concerns the initial choice. Seigneur suggests considering whether making every appliance smart is genuinely useful. If the function is not useful, the connection should not be considered automatic: every connected device adds a new potential attack surface. The checklist thus concludes with a decision before the technical one: protect and update what is connected, but first ask whether it needs to be connected.

## TL;DR - On October 14, 2026, the Federal Council approves Knifefish - Switzerland modernizes its electronic warfare capabilities - Knifefish facilitates procurement and exchanges with European partners - Neutrality remains guaranteed and withdrawal is possible
## Key facts - Decision → Switzerland's accession to the Knifefish MoU - Date → October 14, 2026 - Basic program → Sawfish, Swiss accession in November 2025 - Objective → acquisition of electronic attack systems - Participants → Netherlands, Germany and Denmark - Planned accession → Sweden through an amending agreement
Bern, October 14, 2026. The Federal Council gave its assent to Switzerland's accession to the memorandum of understanding on cooperation for electromagnetic combat capabilities intended for electronic attack, known as the Knifefish MoU.
The measure is part of the modernization of the Swiss Armed Forces' electronic warfare assets. The armed forces need systems capable of detecting, influencing or jamming electromagnetic signals. Switzerland is thus participating in a European program aimed at acquiring electronic attack systems.
### A program built with European partners
With Knifefish, the Netherlands is implementing a program to acquire these systems and facilitate exchanges with European partner states. Germany and Denmark are already participating in the initiative. Sweden intends to join through an amending agreement.
Switzerland's accession to the MoU stems from the Sawfish program, which Switzerland joined in November 2025. The latter concerns tactical electronic warfare systems, while Knifefish concerns electromagnetic combat capabilities for electronic attack.
The Federal Council links this new step to the armaments policy strategy of June 20, 2025. Among other objectives, the strategy provides for a targeted expansion of cooperation with neighboring states and other European partners. The decision of October 14, 2026, therefore brings together three elements already identified in the source: the modernization of the Swiss Armed Forces, European cooperation on procurement, and the connection with the Sawfish program. ## What changes operationally
The most concrete effect described in the press release concerns how military procurement is organized. Cooperation makes it possible to better coordinate materials and data, as well as to jointly use testing equipment and spare parts. For Switzerland, this model may translate into economies of scale and more advantageous purchase prices.
The advantage is not solely economic. Joint procurement strengthens interoperability between Switzerland and the European states participating in the cooperation. The source therefore indicates an operational benefit, linked to the possibility of making materials, data and equipment work together, and a logistical benefit, linked to the shared management of testing and spare parts.
### The three functions of electronic warfare
Electronic warfare uses the electromagnetic spectrum, which includes radio systems, radar and other electromagnetic signals. Its functions are distinct:
| Area | Function | |---|---| | Electronic attack | Reduces the ability of opposing forces to use the electromagnetic spectrum. | | Electronic protection | Protects its own systems from interference. | | Electronic support | Detects and analyzes signals. |
Knifefish concerns electronic attack; the Sawfish program, on the other hand, concerns tactical systems for electronic warfare. This distinction makes it possible to view the accession as an expansion of Swiss cooperation in a sector composed of multiple capabilities, rather than as a single type of equipment.
A precise political clause also remains in place. The MoU allows Switzerland to decide on a case-by-case basis which projects to participate in. Neutrality is guaranteed, and Switzerland may withdraw from the cooperation at any time if one of the states participating in the program becomes involved in an armed conflict. ## How to follow the next steps
The source makes it possible to reconstruct a precise institutional sequence, useful for avoiding confusion between the armament strategy, cooperation programs and individual projects.
### The sequence to follow
1. The first reference is the Federal Council’s strategy on armament policy, dated June 20, 2025. The document provides for targeted expansion of cooperation with neighboring states and other European partners.
2. The second step is Sawfish. Switzerland joined it in November 2025; the program concerns tactical electronic warfare systems.
3. The third reference dates back to October 14, 2026: on that date, the Federal Council approved Switzerland’s accession to the declaration of intent known as MoU Knifefish.
4. For each subsequent project, the case-by-case rule must be taken into account. Accession to the MoU does not automatically determine Swiss participation in every project: the source gives Switzerland the option to choose.
5. Finally, the condition related to neutrality must be verified. If one of the states participating in the program becomes involved in an armed conflict, Switzerland may withdraw from the cooperation at any time.
The certain date to follow is therefore that of the approval on October 14, 2026. The communiqué describes accession to the declaration of intent and the framework for cooperation, while the program’s objective is the acquisition of electronic attack systems. The procedure described is institutional: it concerns the selection of projects, coordination with partner states and the possibility of ending participation under the conditions indicated.
To understand future developments, the safest approach is to keep the three levels separate: the Federal Council’s strategy, the Sawfish program already linked to Switzerland and the new MoU Knifefish. This distinction avoids attributing to the decision content that the source does not indicate.

## Key facts - Location → Canton of Graubünden - Contributions to third parties → +24,8%, amounting to 296,3 million francs - Budget → deficit of almost 100 million francs - Budget item 2023-2027 → +34,5%, amounting to 41,4 million francs - EFAS → almost 20 million francs per year from 2028
The expected deficit of the Canton of Graubünden for next year is close to 100 million francs. The pressure comes as contributions to third parties have increased by 24,8% over the last four years, an absolute increase of 296,3 million francs. Keystone-ATS asked what the reasons for this growth are.
### The items indicated by the Canton During today's press conference, the director of the Graubünden Department of Finance and Municipalities, Martin Bühler (PLR), clarified that the increases are not concentrated in a single area.
Comparing the 2023 actual accounts with the 2027 budget, the budget item recorded growth of 34,5%, amounting to 41,4 million francs. The main factor is individual reductions in health-insurance premiums. Since health-insurance premiums increase every year, the support needed to reduce them for insured persons in modest financial circumstances also grows and, consequently, so does the amount of the Canton's contributions.
In the sector comprising hospitals, healthcare facilities and nursing homes, contributions have grown by 10,9% since 2023. Factors driving expenditure include contributions for medical services governed by the Federal Health Insurance Act, as well as population ageing, a higher hospitalisation rate and the greater average severity of treated cases. From 2028, the transition to uniform financing of outpatient and inpatient services (EFAS) will entail additional costs of almost 20 million francs per year.
Over four years, spending on public transport has increased by 25,51 million francs, or 31,4%. The Canton attributes the increase to a decrease in federal funding and several investment projects, including those concerning Chur West railway station, Tiefencastel station and the Ilanz/Glion bus terminal. Moreover, in 2027, the implementation of Simon Gredig's (Greens) motion will affect costs and entail the transfer of burdens from the municipalities to the Canton, amounting to three million francs for 2027 and 2028.
For special education, the financial burden has grown by 45,5%, or 25 million francs. ## Reading budget pressure The increase in contributions to third parties should be read as the sum of different mechanisms. For anyone following a canton's accounts, the first practical distinction is between premium subsidies, healthcare services, regional transport and special education: the source brings them together in the same dynamic, but attributes different causes to each.
### Four mechanisms to separate | Item | Mechanism indicated | Time horizon | |---|---|---| | Individual premium reductions | Health-insurance premiums increasing and support for policyholders in modest economic circumstances | 2023 final accounts and 2027 budget | | Hospitals, healthcare facilities and nursing homes | Aging, higher hospitalization and greater severity of cases | From 2028 with EFAS | | Public transport | Reduction in federal funding and investment projects | 2027 and 2028 | | Special education | Integration projects, new jobs and employment percentages | Four-year period |
This separation avoids confusing premium growth with hospital expenditure. In the first case, the chain described is linear: rising health-insurance premiums, higher individual reductions and a greater cantonal contribution for insured persons in modest economic circumstances. The figure therefore concerns the relationship between premiums and support, not a single investment project.
For hospitals and nursing homes, the indicated factor is demographic and clinical: population aging is associated with a higher hospitalization rate and greater average severity of the cases treated. The outlook changes from 2028, when EFAS will entail almost 20 million francs per year in additional costs in the sector.
In public transport, the reading must take funding and investments together. The reduction in federal funding is indicated as the cause of the increase; several projects are cited in the same sector. The 2027 motion also makes the financial relationship between the Canton and the municipalities visible: the message quantifies the transfer of costs from the municipalities to the Canton at three million for 2027 and three million for 2028.
Special education follows a different trajectory: the Canton links the increase to the growth of integration projects, the creation of jobs and staff employment percentages. To read the budget without losing the causal link, it is therefore advisable to examine separately the item, the indicated cause and the year in which the increase has an impact. This breakdown shows how costs are distributed among insured persons, healthcare facilities, transport, municipalities and special education services. ## A practical procedure To follow the message about the budget without mixing data from different periods, the reader can use a simple sequence. The starting point is the time references cited by the source: 2023 actuals, 2027 budget and 2028 outlook.
### Four steps 1. Put the 2023 actuals in a first column and the 2027 budget in a second. This keeps the comparison anchored to the period used for the budget item that increased by 34,5%, amounting to 41,4 million francs. It should not be confused with the overall figure for contributions to third parties over the last four years.
2. Divide the items by cause. For individual premium reductions, note the annual increase in health-insurance premiums and the reference to policyholders in modest financial circumstances. For hospitals, healthcare facilities and nursing homes, note instead medical services, population ageing, hospitalisation and severity of cases.
3. Open a separate section for public transport. This should record the reduction in federal funding, the Chur West railway station, Tiefencastel station and Ilanz/Glion bus terminal projects, as well as the motion implemented in 2027. The transfer of costs indicated for the Canton is three million francs in 2027 and three million francs in 2028.
4. Keep the 2028 outlook distinct. The transition to EFAS will entail additional costs of almost 20 million francs per year in the healthcare sector. For special education, however, the review must instead follow integration projects, new jobs and staff employment percentages.
This framework helps prevent chapters that the Canton describes separately from being read as a single expense. For policyholders interested in the evolution of premiums, the operational step is to compare the health insurers with compare the health insurers.

item.title: Unpaid fines? Here’s who can save you from prison
item.description: Freiheitsfonds has raised almost 100'000 francs.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Freiheitsfonds has raised nearly 100'000 francs. - 47 people have avoided a total of 451 days in prison. - In 2024, there were 3'935 admissions for substitute sentences. - Substitute detention can last up to 90 days. ## Key facts - Fund → Freiheitsfonds - Funds raised → almost 100'000 francs - Beneficiaries → 47 people - Detention avoided → 451 days - Conversion → up to 90 days of detention - 2024 figure → 3'935 prison admissions - Zurich study → 69% for traffic or public transport violations - Estimated cost → 200-300 francs per day Data from the Federal Statistical Office indicate that in 2024, prison admissions in Switzerland for the enforcement of substitute sentences totaled 3'935, more than four times the number recorded in 2000. This figure highlights the problem addressed by Freiheitsfonds, the Swiss fund that pays the penalties of people who cannot afford them. Donations enabled the fund to raise almost 100'000 francs, which has already paid the penalties of 47 people. In total, the intervention avoided 451 days of detention, according to the NZZ. ### How substitute sentences work Failure to pay a fine or monetary penalty may lead to its conversion into a substitute custodial sentence lasting up to 90 days. This is a controversial mechanism, since it risks disproportionately affecting people facing financial difficulties and contributes to filling prisons. According to a study conducted in Zurich in 2019, 69% of those interviewed had received a penalty for violations related to traffic or public transport. In Parliament, the National Council rejected the proposal by Jessica Jaccoud, a Vaud Socialist National Councillor, which aimed to replace detention for unpaid fines of up to 5'000 francs with other measures. The fund believes that intervening before imprisonment is also economically worthwhile: according to the estimates cited, a day in detention costs 200-300 francs. The issue nevertheless continues to raise doubts. There are fears that intervention by a private party could weaken the enforcement of penalties and the deterrent effect of fines; moreover, people who travel without a ticket may not do so exclusively for financial reasons. Among the alternatives already provided for is community service, the organization of which can nevertheless prove complex. Zurich has a dedicated service; Bern, by contrast, wants to extend the use of this measure to cases in which the sentence has already been converted into detention. Finally, some municipalities suggest not filing criminal complaints against people who travel without a valid ticket, focusing instead on the surcharge and debt recovery. ## Three paths with different effects For people living in Switzerland, the issue is not limited to the amount of the penalty. The source compares three paths: conversion into substitute detention, community service and, in some cases of travelling without a valid ticket, a surcharge and debt recovery instead of a criminal complaint. ### The practical comparison | Path | What it entails according to the source | |---|---| | Unpaid fine or monetary penalty | Possible conversion into a substitute custodial sentence of up to 90 days | | Community service | An alternative already provided for, but not always easy to organize | | Travel without a valid ticket | In some municipalities, foregoing a criminal complaint, a surcharge and debt recovery | The first path is the one that turns non-payment into possible detention. The second keeps the response in the realm of community service, but applying it requires an organizational setup that the source describes as not always easy. The third concerns a narrower scope: travel without a valid ticket and proposals from some municipalities. The difference between the three paths has an immediate practical effect. According to its objective, the Freiheitsfonds intervenes before incarceration; community service is indicated as an alternative; the municipal transport model instead focuses on the surcharge and debt recovery. They are different responses to the same problem of non-payment, but they are not interchangeable. ### Where Zurich and Bern fit in Zurich has a service dedicated to community service. In Bern, the aim is to extend the use of this measure to sentences already converted into detention. The source therefore presents an existing service and an announced extension, not a single procedure described for all territories. From an economic perspective, the fund argues that intervention before detention makes sense because one day in prison is estimated to cost between 200 and 300 francs. As for the concerns, there remains a fear that a private entity could weaken enforcement of sanctions and reduce the deterrent effect of fines. The same source points out that financial difficulties do not necessarily explain every journey without a ticket. The practical picture therefore requires distinguishing between the type of sanction, the point at which conversion takes place, and the alternative provided for in the territory in question. A municipal transport proposal is not equivalent to private payment of a sanction, while community service is not the same as substitute detention. ## Navigating without adding unmentioned rules The source does not describe a single form, deadline or office for requesting assistance from the Freiheitsfonds. The practical steps that can therefore be reconstructed are linked to the type of sanction and the stage the case has reached. ### Four steps 1. Distinguish the sanction. The text considers both the fine and the monetary penalty. When they are not paid, they can be converted into a substitute custodial sentence, up to 90 days. 2. Place the case before imprisonment. The fund’s stated objective is to pay the sanctions of people at risk of prison because they cannot afford them. The source documents assistance for 47 people, but does not describe a general access procedure: it is therefore not possible to derive a form or deadline from the text. 3. Consider community service: the system already provides for it, but its organization is not always simple. The example cited is Zurich, which has a dedicated service; Bern aims to extend this option to sentences already converted into detention. 4. Separate public transport cases. For people travelling without a valid ticket, some municipalities propose waiving the criminal complaint and focusing on the surcharge and debt recovery. The proposal is linked to that type of offence and should not automatically be extended to every fine. ### The limits of the available information The text does not indicate a uniform procedure throughout Switzerland, nor does it establish that the fund pays every unpaid sanction. Instead, it reports an objective, some results and alternatives located in Zurich, Bern or unspecified municipalities. For the reader, the decisive distinction is therefore between an unpaid sanction, possible conversion, community service and the municipal model applied to travelling without a valid ticket. ## TL;DR - Plurilateral Agreement on Electronic Commerce at the WTO - 67 members, including Switzerland, choose provisional implementation - Consultation from 14 October 2026 to 28 January 2027
## Key facts - Subject: plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce - Negotiations: concluded in 2024 within the WTO - Decision: 28 March 2026, 14th ordinary session - Participants: 67 members, including Switzerland - Instrument: Annex on provisional provisions - Objective: to simplify digital trade and strengthen legal certainty - Start of consultation: 14 October 2026 - Consultation deadline: 28 January 2027
## The decision and the consultation
Switzerland will open a consultation on the plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce on 14 October 2026. The text concerns a negotiation conducted within the WTO and already completed in 2024. The opening is communicated by the Federal Department of Economy, Education and Research, indicated in the official communication.
On 28 March 2026, at the 14th (regular) session of the WTO Ministerial Conference, 67 members, including Switzerland, opted for the application of the Agreement through an Annex on provisional provisions. The initiative does not yet equate to the formal inclusion of the agreement in the WTO legal framework: for now, the provisional regime adopted by the members remains distinct from the legal milestone envisaged for the agreement.
### An agreement still in the integration phase
The objective remains the formal inclusion of the agreement in Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement. According to the communication, this step is currently blocked by some WTO members. For this reason, the text describes a provisional solution already chosen by the 67 participants and, in parallel, a broader legal objective that has not yet been achieved. Switzerland appears among the members who have decided on implementation via the annex on provisional provisions, while the formalization is indicated as still blocked.
The calendar allows us to distinguish three moments. Negotiations within the WTO concluded in 2024; on 28 March 2026 the 67 members decided on implementation through the Annex on Interim Provisions; the consultation starts on 14 October 2026. They are different passages, with different functions in the text: the first concerns the end of the negotiations, the second the provisional arrangement, the third the time window communicated for the Swiss consultation. The consultation ends on 28 January 2027.
For those observing the Swiss economy, the concrete point indicated by the source is the objective of simplifying digital trade between members and, at the same time, strengthening legal certainty. The communication does not announce new operational rules, amounts or obligations for businesses and consumers. Furthermore, it does not provide a timetable after 28 January 2027. The article can therefore record the consultation and its scope, without transforming it into a modification that has already entered into force. ## Effects to be read with caution
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the news should be read as an institutional step, not as the announcement of a new immediate fulfillment. The source talks about an agreement intended to simplify digital trade between members and strengthen legal certainty, but does not list specific operational changes for online sales. Without these details, it is not possible to derive a new obligation for a Swiss operator from the communication.
### The value of distinction
The practical utility of news lies in separating what is already decided from what remains a goal. The decision of the 67 members concerns the implementation through an annex on the provisional provisions. The formal integration in Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement is instead described as still blocked by some WTO members. For a company that follows digital trade, this difference prevents it from presenting the agreement as a framework definitively integrated into the WTO system.
The source does not quantify the expected benefit and does not indicate which sectors, business size or categories of users would be involved first. The only declared effect is the general direction: to make digital trade between members easier and to increase legal certainty. Any assessment of costs, time, documents or procedures would require elements that do not appear in the communication.
### The comparison between the scenarios
The scenario described today combines a provisional implementation decision and a formal integration still blocked. If the block indicated by the source remained, the text would continue to distinguish these two planes; if the formal integration was achieved, the stated objective would have a different outcome. However, the source does not allow to attribute a date or a result to either scenario.
For this reason, the deadline of 28 January 2027 is above all the point of control of the consultation. It is not presented as the date of entry into force of the agreement, nor as the term for a new commercial obligation. Those working on Swiss digital exchanges can use this distinction to avoid premature conclusions. ## Follow the procedure:
Those who want to follow the consultation can start from an essential chronology, without overlapping the stages. The communication provides the dates, the object and the objective of the dossier. For any contributions, you must follow the instructions of the official documentation associated with the consultation; the article does not allow you to add channels or forms not indicated.
### Five operational checks
1. Identify the subject: plurilateral agreement on electronic commerce, negotiated within the framework of the WTO. 2. Rebuild the previous step: the negotiations were completed in 2024. 3. Record the decision of 28 March 2026: 67 members, including Switzerland, chose implementation by means of an annex on interim provisions. 4. Verify the perimeter: the objective remains the formal integration in Annex 4 of the WTO Agreement, currently blocked by some WTO members. 5. Mark the Swiss window: start on 14 October 2026, end on 28 January 2027.
For those preparing an analysis or intending to participate in the consultation, the most prudent line is to focus on the two stated objectives: simplifying digital trade between members and strengthening legal certainty. The material provided does not authorize to present as already defined new rates, forms, obligations, sanctions or deadlines other than January 28, 2027. Nor does it allow you to describe the formal integration as already approved.
After the end, the source does not indicate a date for the next step. The control to be done is therefore concrete: check if the official documentation associated with the consultation adds procedural instructions and follow any further communications on integration into the WTO. Until then, the verifiable basis remains the provisional decision of the 67 members and the consultation opened in Switzerland. This method makes it possible to distinguish a consultation deadline from an application date, a distinction that the text of the news item maintains.

## TL;DR - The Federal Council launches the consultation on October 14, 2026 - The project concerns a total revision of customs law - The consultation period ends on January 28, 2027 - The focus is the new ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC
## Key facts - What → Total revision of customs law - Who → Federal Council - When → October 14, 2026 - Deadline → January 28, 2027 - Legal bases → LUDSC and LTDo - Program → DaziT - Parliament → June 20, 2025
The Federal Council launched the consultation procedure on October 14, 2026, at its meeting in Bern, on the package of ordinances for the total revision of customs law. The decision concerns the comprehensive modernization of the legal bases and forms part of the DaziT digitalization and transformation program, also linking to the development of the organization of the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (UDSC).
### A new framework ordinance
The core of the project is the creation of a new framework ordinance: the ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC. The text aims to reduce the administrative burden for the economy and clarify the methods for harmonizing and digitalizing procedures. Simplifications are also planned for the collection of duties and for the activities through which the UDSC manages and controls the cross-border movement of goods and people.
The federal communication therefore presents a framework that combines organization, procedures and duties. The package is intended to give concrete form to the new customs legislation through several implementing acts. The consultation concerns the preliminary drafts and the documentation published for the recipients identified in the procedure.
### The ordinances involved
Numerous ordinances are undergoing a total revision. The ordinance on customs will become the new ordinance on customs duties. The package also includes the ordinance on tobacco taxation, the ordinance on beer, the ordinance on motor vehicles, the ordinance on mineral oils and the ordinance on alcohol.
The timetable sets the close of the consultation for January 28, 2027. The amendments implement the LUDSC and the new LTDo through ordinances, adopted by Parliament on June 20, 2025. The LTDo governs customs duties, while the LUDSC consolidates and standardizes the UDSC's enforcement tasks in a single separate framework law.
The new provisions create the stated legal bases for simplifying, harmonizing and digitalizing customs and duty-collection processes on a large scale. The publication of October 14, 2026 accompanies the opening with the preliminary drafts, explanatory reports, a letter to the Cantons, a letter to organizations and the list of recipients of the procedure. ## What it means for procedures
For companies and operators handling goods or people across the border, the most concrete point indicated by the Federal Council is not a new amount, but how the procedures should be organized. The source links the new ordinance to three objectives: reducing the administrative burden, harmonizing the steps and digitizing the procedures. These objectives are aimed at the economy and the UDSC's activities. However, the press release does not indicate figures, rates or savings timelines.
This limitation is relevant to a practical reading of the dossier. The text announces a total revision and puts preliminary drafts out for consultation, but does not present a list of new obligations to be fulfilled immediately. The most prudent implication for those operating in cross-border traffic is therefore to distinguish between the project's stated direction and the applicable rules described in the press release.
### Comparison between the current and proposed frameworks
The comparison that can be made concerns primarily the structure of the rules. The legislation approved by Parliament separates the rules governing customs duties, contained in the LTDo, from the UDSC's implementation tasks, set out in the LUDSC. The package of ordinances reflects this distinction: the customs ordinance is transformed into an ordinance on customs duties, while a new framework ordinance specifies the office's tasks and the manner in which procedures are conducted.
| Scope | Reference cited | Project direction | |---|---|---| | Customs duties | LTDo and ordinance on customs duties | Revision of the implementing rules | | UDSC tasks | LUDSC and ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC | Harmonization through a framework law and the ordinances | | Processes | DaziT Programme | Digitalization, simplification and harmonization |
### What remains to be verified
The ordinances on the taxation of tobacco, beer, motor vehicles, mineral oils and alcohol are included in the package, but the press release does not indicate specific changes for each duty. The source therefore provides no new amounts or new rates to apply. The consultation is the step explicitly communicated and closes on January 28, 2027.
The dossier is also accompanied by a letter to the cantons, a letter to organizations and a list of recipients. These documents are part of the official publication together with the texts and explanatory reports. For families, workers and businesses, the concrete point is therefore the launch of a broad regulatory revision, with procedural effects still to be defined through the documents submitted for consultation. ## How to follow the consultation
To read the dossier in an orderly manner, the process can be organized into five steps based on the materials provided:
1. Mark January 28, 2027 as the deadline for the consultation procedure. 2. Open the draft ordinances published on October 14, 2026. 3. Read the explanatory reports on the total revision alongside the texts. 4. Consult the letter to the Cantons, the letter to the organizations and the list of recipients. 5. Compare the ordinances with the LUDSC and LTDo adopted by Parliament on June 20, 2025.
The first reading criterion is the subject of the dossier. For the tasks and controls of the UDSC, start with the ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC, that is, the new framework ordinance. For the regulation of customs duties, the reference is the ordinance on customs duties, intended to replace the Customs Ordinance as part of the total revision.
A second approach concerns specific levies. The package includes texts relating to tobacco, beer, motor vehicles, mineral oils and alcohol. It is therefore advisable to associate each topic with the relevant draft ordinance and corresponding explanatory report, without confusing these ordinances with the general ordinance on the tasks of the UDSC.

The same publication lists the documents addressed to the Cantons and organizations and makes the list of recipients of the procedure available.
For those following the dossier from the perspective of the economy or cross-border traffic, this sequence avoids reading a single ordinance in isolation. The DaziT program in fact links the digitalization, simplification and harmonization of customs and duty collection processes. The deadline indicated by the Federal Council remains January 28, 2027; until that date, the official material to be examined is that of the consultation launched on October 14, 2026.

## TL;DR - Alliance Care closes and initiates bankruptcy proceedings - The decision was made in Bern - 17 layoffs out of 91 employees - ASI had granted loans
## Key facts - Organization → Alliance Care - Decision → cessation of operations and bankruptcy proceedings - Founded → June 2025 - Staff → 91 employees; 17 laid off - Stabilization → efforts launched in April 2026 - Members → memberships below expectations - Support → loans from Associazione svizzera infermieri - Report → July investigation in Tamedia group newspapers
Alliance Care is ceasing its activities and initiating bankruptcy proceedings. In Bern, the nursing council and the assembly of delegates adopted the decision after an in-depth discussion.
The organization cites financial difficulties as the cause of the closure. Financial results were below expectations, and the measures launched in April 2026 to stabilize the accounts did not make it possible to ensure continuity of operations.
### A crisis that emerged in stages
In June, the first signs of the crisis had already emerged, with 17 of Alliance Care's 91 employees being laid off. Associazione svizzera infermieri, which promoted the project, had sought to provide financial support to the new organization through several loans. Despite this, the financial problems had not been resolved.
The failure to increase membership was another factor. Growth in new members was one of the foundations of the association's development prospects, but membership did not reach the hoped-for levels. Alliance Care thus became unable to ensure long-term financial stability. The difficulties affected both the accounts and the expected membership growth.
An investigation published last July by the newspapers of the Tamedia group had shown that membership was significantly below forecasts. This was part of the series of difficulties that culminated in today's decision.
Founded in June 2025, Alliance Care aimed to bring together in a single organization all professionals in the care sector, including healthcare workers without a nursing diploma. Just over a year after its founding, the representation project is closing with the initiation of bankruptcy proceedings. ## What it means for healthcare representation
The bankruptcy of Alliance Care brings to an end an organizational project designed to broaden the representation of healthcare personnel. The source links that project to two precise conditions: the ability to support the finances and the arrival of new members. When membership remained below expectations, the prospect of long-term financial stability disappeared.
### Before and after
Before the decision, Alliance Care was supposed to bring together under one roof all care professionals, including healthcare workers without a nursing diploma. After the decision of the nursing council and the assembly of delegates, that objective will not continue through the organization. For those working in the sector, the news should be read as the conclusion of a specific association model, not as a change to the professional activities described in the source.
The comparison can be summarized as follows: - the project aimed at broader representation; - the arrival of new members was part of the development prospects; - financial results and membership numbers did not reach the necessary levels.
This sequence also clarifies the role of the Swiss Nurses Association. As its promoter, ASI had granted loans to the new organization. The source specifies, however, that these measures were not enough to resolve the economic problems. The initial support, therefore, did not enable Alliance Care to achieve the financial stability it was seeking.
The figure for employees should be read without additions. The 17 layoffs out of 91 people are the number indicated for June, when the first signs of the crisis had already emerged. The text does not make it possible to infer any other employment outcomes, nor to establish what the position of the staff not involved in those layoffs will be.
For members as well, the source establishes one point, but does not describe subsequent steps: membership was below expectations and this affected long-term prospects. No methods of reimbursement, transfer, or continuation of individual memberships are indicated. The practical takeaway therefore remains limited to the end of the organization and the initiation of bankruptcy proceedings. ## What to do now

item.title: Swisscom fine annulled: COMCO assesses the appeal
item.description: The TAF annuls Swisscom’s 18,4 million fine.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - TAF annuls Swisscom's fine of 18,4 million francs - The penalty was imposed in December 2023 - COMCO is considering whether to appeal to the Federal Supreme Court
## Key facts - Subject → fiber-optic dispute - Penalty → 18,4 million francs - Date of penalty → December 2023 - COMCO investigation → launched at the end of 2020 - Next step → analysis of the ruling in the coming days - Possible outcomes → acceptance or appeal to the Federal Supreme Court
### The course of the dispute
18,4 million francs: that is the amount of the fine that the Federal Administrative Court annulled in the ruling made public yesterday evening. The penalty had been imposed on Swisscom in December 2023 and arose from the fiber-optic dispute.
The FAC did not find that the telecom operator held a dominant position. This conclusion differs from that of the Competition Commission, which had argued that there was a dominant position and had launched an investigation into the case at the end of 2020. That investigation then culminated in the penalty imposed in December 2023.
The central issue in the matter is therefore the interpretation of a dominant position in the telecommunications sector. On the one hand, there is COMCO's assessment, which led to the fine; on the other, that of the FAC judges, who did not recognize that position and annulled the penalty.
The proceedings do not necessarily end with the ruling made public yesterday evening. COMCO told the Awp news agency that it would examine the judgment in depth in the coming days. Only after this analysis will the authority decide how to proceed.
The two options indicated are clear-cut: accept the judgment of the Federal Administrative Court or appeal to the Federal Supreme Court. In the first case, COMCO accepts the FAC's decision. In the second, the fiber-optic dispute continues before the court indicated by the authority itself.
The report therefore describes one step that has already been decided and another that remains open. The decided step is the annulment of the fine of 18,4 million francs. The open one concerns the Competition Commission's response, expected after the analysis announced for the coming days. ## The practical takeaway for the telecom sector
The judgment has a concrete effect on the proceedings: the fine imposed on Swisscom in December 2023 has been annulled. Its significance, however, must be considered together with the decision that COMCO still has to make. The same dispute remains tied to two different interpretations of the dominant position in the telecom sector: the one supported by the authority and the one accepted by the Federal Administrative Court.
For people who live or work in Switzerland, the practical takeaway is not an already announced change to bills, contracts, plans, speeds or coverage. The source does not report changes of this kind. Automatically linking the annulment of the penalty to savings for users or a deterioration in service would therefore go beyond the available information.
### Two scenarios for the national perspective
The first scenario is acceptance of the judgment. In this case, COMCO would not file the appeal mentioned in the news report, and the case would remain governed by the TAF's judgment, which found that Swisscom did not hold a dominant position.
The second scenario is an appeal to the Federal Supreme Court. Here, the point to watch would not be a new fine already decided, but the continuation of the dispute over the interpretation of the dominant position and fiber optics. The source does not anticipate which option will be chosen or what the outcome of any appeal would be.
The difference between before and after the judgment is therefore primarily procedural. Before, COMCO's position had led to an investigation launched in late 2020 and to the penalty in December 2023. After the decision made public yesterday evening, that fine was annulled by the TAF, and the authority must consider its next step.
This is also the useful framework for interpreting any reactions in the telecommunications sector. The verified fact concerns the penalty, the dispute over fiber optics, and the interpretation of the dominant position. The source contains no figures on prices, investments, customers, or commercial terms. The national significance of the news is therefore tied to the process involving COMCO, TAF, and possible involvement of the Federal Supreme Court, not to an announced change in tariffs. ## How to follow the case without anticipating the outcomes
To correctly understand the next developments, it is useful to separate the outcome of the judgment from the decision still awaited from COMCO. The former is already known; the latter has yet to arrive.
### Monitoring procedure
1. Establish the current status: the Federal Administrative Court annulled the fine of 18,4 million francs imposed on Swisscom in December 2023.
2. Identify the subject: the matter concerns the dispute over fiber optics and the dominant position in the telecommunications sector. It should not be turned into an announcement about tariffs or services, because the source contains no indications of this kind.
3. Await the step indicated by COMCO: the authority said it will examine the judgment thoroughly in the coming days. No precise date is reported, so a different deadline should not be added.
4. Distinguish between the two outcomes: COMCO may accept the TAF's ruling or file an appeal with the Federal Supreme Court. These are the only avenues indicated in the report.
This framework also avoids a frequent error in reading the case: confusing the annulment of the sanction with the already definitive conclusion of every step. The TAF's judgment resulted in the annulment of the fine, but COMCO still has to announce whether it accepts the ruling or chooses to appeal.
The source does not indicate any forms to fill out, documents to submit, or obligations for residents and workers. There is therefore no individual procedure to initiate in order to follow the case. The concrete action consists of checking what decision the Competition Commission will make after the announced analysis and keeping the facts already established separate from any possible future consequences.
Until COMCO's choice is indicated, the information to use is that of the judgment made public last night: the fine was annulled, and the issue of the dominant position remains at the center of the dispute over fiber optics.

item.description: IMF and World Bank summit in Bangkok from October 15 to 17, 2026 Parmelin, Keller-Sutter and Schlegel in the Swiss delegation New partnership agreement
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - IMF and World Bank summit in Bangkok from October 15 to 17, 2026 - Parmelin, Keller-Sutter and Schlegel in the Swiss delegation - New Swiss partnership agreement with the IMF - 40 million francs to the IMF for the 2026–2030 period
## Key facts - Date of the communiqué → October 14, 2026 - Venue and dates → Bangkok, from October 15 to 17, 2026 - Participants → Guy Parmelin, Karin Keller-Sutter, Martin Schlegel - Partnership → approved by the Federal Council on August 26, 2026 - Amount → 40 million francs for the 2026–2030 period
On October 14, 2026, from Bern, the Confederation announced Switzerland’s participation in the annual meeting of the IMF and World Bank, scheduled to take place in Bangkok from October 15 to 17, 2026. The meeting will be attended by President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin, Federal Councillor Karin Keller-Sutter, and Martin Schlegel, President of the Swiss National Bank.
During the same summit, the G20 finance ministers will meet with central bank governors. The Swiss delegation will also use the opportunity to hold bilateral talks.
### The Confederation’s position
The meetings will address current global challenges facing the economy and development policy. The communiqué emphasizes that persistent geopolitical tensions and trade conflicts are weighing on the global economy. Switzerland is committed to reliable international economic relations, open markets and resilient supply chains.
The position also lists three conditions for resilience and growth: sound public finances, financial stability and integrity, as well as an economic policy conducive to innovation. With regard to the IMF, Switzerland calls for qualified and independent advice focused on fundamental risks and core competencies. It also supports comprehensive and objective assessments of member countries’ positions on external economic policy, prudent lending and sound Fund finances.
The World Bank is viewed positively for its greater focus on jobs and private investment. The stated priority remains development impact and the fight against poverty, with favorable economic framework conditions, effective and inclusive labor markets, and high environmental and social standards.
Finally, Switzerland will sign a new partnership agreement with the IMF; the Federal Council approved it on August 26, 2026. Implemented by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, the partnership allocates 40 million francs over the 2026–2030 period to technical assistance for building capacity and state institutions in member countries. At the G20, under the presidency of the United States, Switzerland will support economic openness, reliable and growth-friendly framework conditions, as well as greater debt transparency and more effective conversions in emerging and developing countries. For Swiss companies and investors, the news is primarily about positioning. The statement links Switzerland’s ongoing commitment to strengthening its position within the IMF and the World Bank and points to two possible benefits: more favorable conditions for trade and investment and lower exposure to economic risks.
The partnership amount should be read together with its intended use. The 40 million francs earmarked for the 2026–2030 period will fund IMF technical assistance to build capacity and state institutions in member countries. For a Swiss operator, the practical takeaway is therefore to observe whether this funding line helps make international markets more reliable, rather than treating the amount as directly available for individual activities.
### Three indicators to watch
| Signal | Outcome sought by Switzerland’s position | |---|---| | Open markets | Reliable international economic relations | | Resilient supply chains | Lower exposure to economic risks | | Sound public finances, stability and financial integrity | Resilience and growth | | Jobs and private investment | Development impact |
This framework shifts attention from the individual allocation to system-level results. The source links sound public finances, stability and financial integrity to resilience and growth; for the World Bank, it instead links jobs, the mobilization of private investment, the fight against poverty and development impact. Effective and inclusive labor markets and high environmental and social standards are identified as framework conditions.
Geopolitical tensions and trade conflicts are described as pressures on the global economy. The announced Swiss response focuses on economic openness, resilient supply chains and reliable, growth-friendly framework conditions. This approach is relevant to companies exposed to trade and investment, but the statement does not anticipate sector-specific results or immediate effects. For this reason too, the bilateral talks in Bangkok should be distinguished from the general objectives: the source announces that they will take place, but does not report their outcome.
Debt transparency and more effective conversions in emerging and developing countries round out Switzerland’s position at the G20. For the domestic reader, the practical key is to check in future updates whether the stated priorities become more reliable economic conditions, without turning a negotiating objective into an already-achieved result. To follow the matter without confusing announcements and results, a company, investor, or reader can create a monitoring sheet. It serves to separate what is already planned from what the delegation will seek to support.
### Five operational steps
1. Set the dates: October 15–17, 2026 for Bangkok, August 26, 2026 for the approval of the partnership, and 2026–2030 for the planned period. 2. Divide the dossiers: IMF and World Bank on one side, the G20 meeting on the other. This way, you do not attribute partnership decisions to the G20. 3. Record updates under Swiss priorities: open markets, resilient supply chains, sound public finances, financial stability and integrity, innovation, jobs, and private investment. 4. Link the news to trade relations and investments that depend on reliable international economic conditions. 5. After Bangkok, look for the outcomes of bilateral talks and developments on debt and conversions in emerging and developing countries.
Keep established facts, such as the approval of the new agreement, separate from the negotiating positions that Switzerland intends to support at the G20.
The amount of 40 million francs should be understood in light of its purpose: IMF technical assistance for capacity-building and state institutions in member countries. The press release links it to the partnership implemented by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs, not to an individual benefit.
For a company, verification consists of comparing updates against three questions: Are trade conditions becoming more favorable? Are the supply chains proving more resilient? Is the lower exposure to economic risks being documented? For an investor, the same framework helps avoid treating stated objectives as results already achieved.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the national perspective therefore comes through subsequent documents: what framework conditions emerge, what effects are documented for trade and investment, and which commitments move from position to implementation. The meeting provides the dates to get started; the press release does not anticipate the outcomes.
To connect economic scenarios to your daily budget, consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
